_comment: Allow-list of intentional Playwright skips. Every `test.skip(condition, reason)` reason in frontend/e2e must have an entry here (exact `match` or regex `pattern`); the nightly email flags any reason it cannot classify. `expected` is the per-project count of tests this reason skips on a full-matrix run; `expected_total: 0` marks reasons that should never fire on a nightly run and are anomalies when they do. Update this file in the same PR that adds or removes specs.

reasons.match: the axe baseline is recorded and replayed on chromium only
reasons.explain: The axe accessibility baseline was recorded on Chromium. Axe rules are engine-independent, so replaying it on three more engines would only add minutes.

reasons.match: drag characterization is recorded and replayed on chromium only
reasons.explain: The drag-and-drop golden needs faithful synthetic pointer events, which differ per engine; the rules it checks do not, and phones render a plain grid anyway.

reasons.match: token resolution is engine-independent; checked on chromium only
reasons.explain: CSS custom-property resolution and the look/mode axe sweep do not vary by engine, so one run on Chromium is the whole answer.

reasons.match: shell layout is engine-independent; checked on chromium only
reasons.explain: Nav, command palette and drawer behaviour touches no store or network and renders identically across engines.

reasons.match: custom-property resolution is engine-independent; checked on chromium only
reasons.explain: The --chart-* token check on /liquidity is the same computation in every engine.

reasons.match: a pure comparison needs checking once, not once per engine
reasons.explain: Pure unit tests of the axe regression comparator; no browser is involved at all.

reasons.pattern: performance entries are Chromium's; this test runs on chromium only
reasons.explain: Long-task and layout-shift PerformanceObserver entries exist only in Chromium, so the perf checks cannot measure anything elsewhere.

reasons.pattern: performance entries are Chromium's; this test runs on chromium-motion only
reasons.explain: The two @motion board perf checks must measure with animations live, so they belong to the chromium-motion project and skip on the four reduced-motion projects.

reasons.match: the motion-on guard; the other projects run with reducedMotion: reduce
reasons.explain: GSAP is inert under reducedMotion: reduce, so the leaked-tween guard only means something on the motion-enabled project.
mouse.wheel is a Chromium capability; the sibling structural test covers the scroll trap on every engine. Pixel 7 reports itself as Chromium, so only the WebKit projects skip.

reasons.match: the header overflows this device, so the page is zoomed out and its controls cannot be driven
reasons.explain: Fires only when the liquidity header overflows a phone viewport and the page zooms out. The UI overhaul fixed the overflow; if this reappears the header has regressed.
The bundle-size check needs the production build that the suite's webServer produces. A nightly run always has it; this firing means the build step was skipped.
